cards.title: Orienting yourself in the Shopify admin navigation
cards.summary: Learn the left-hand admin map so you can find product, order, market and analytics functions without hunting.
cards.use_when: You are new to Shopify admin or onboarding a staff member and need to know where each store operation lives.

cards.title: Create Physical Products with Weight to Enable Shipping
cards.summary: Turning on product weight is required so Shopify treats an item as physical and offers shipping rates.
cards.use_when: Adding a new physical product in Shopify admin and configuring shipping eligibility.

cards.title: Set Up Product Variants for Size and Color
cards.summary: Add variant options so one product listing offers all sizes and colors with per-variant pricing, stock, and images.
cards.use_when: Listing apparel or any product that comes in multiple sizes, colors, or materials.

cards.title: Build Manual vs Smart Collections
cards.summary: Smart collections auto-populate by rules like tags, vendor, price, or inventory, and the type is locked once created.
cards.use_when: Organizing a catalog into collections that stay current as products are added.

cards.title: Tag Products Consistently for Smart Collections
cards.summary: Standardized product tags drive reliable smart collections, and inconsistent spelling silently excludes products.
cards.use_when: Assigning tags to products so collections, filters, and navigation stay organized.

cards.title: Use Bulk Edit for Prices, Quantities, and Tags
cards.summary: Shopify's spreadsheet-style bulk editor updates many products at once but has limits that may require a third-party app.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up prices, stock levels, or tags across a large product catalog.

cards.title: Edit Product Images In-Shopify: Crop, Resize, Remove Background
cards.summary: Shopify's built-in image tools handle cropping, resizing, background removal, and background generation at the product level.
cards.use_when: Fixing inconsistent product photos or making PDP images match your visual standards without external tools.

cards.title: Generate Product Images with Sidekick AI
cards.summary: Shopify's Sidekick can generate lifestyle product images from a product photo and a prompt, iterating conversationally.
cards.use_when: Creating lifestyle or contextual imagery for product pages or ads when you lack photoshoots.

cards.title: Configure Variant Color Swatches with Hex or Pattern Images
cards.summary: Shopify assigns default variant colors from category meta fields; you can override with exact hex codes or pattern images.
cards.use_when: Setting up color swatches for a product where default swatch colors are inaccurate or you sell patterns/textures.

cards.title: Set Up Storefront Filters with the Search and Discovery App
cards.summary: Shopify's free Search and Discovery app controls which filters (price, availability, category meta fields, or custom) appear on collection pages.
cards.use_when: Adding filterable navigation to a collection page so shoppers can narrow a large catalog by attributes.

cards.title: Create Custom Product Filters When Category Meta Fields Fall Short
cards.summary: Custom product meta fields let you add filters beyond Shopify's category defaults and apply them across all products.
cards.use_when: Adding a filter attribute your niche needs that isn't in the default category meta fields.

cards.title: Choose Filters from Customer Search Language
cards.summary: Filters should reflect how shoppers search and what competitors in the niche expose, not every attribute you have.
cards.use_when: Deciding which filters to expose on category pages for a new or existing store.

cards.title: Filter Shopify Themes by Industry, Catalog Size, and Required Features
cards.summary: Use Shopify theme store filters to narrow hundreds of themes down to a shortlist matching your niche, catalog size, and required sections.
cards.use_when: Shortlisting candidate Shopify themes before committing to a design foundation.

cards.title: Preview Mobile and Desktop Before Buying a Theme
cards.summary: Always check a theme's mobile demo since most traffic is mobile, and shortlist only themes whose mobile experience holds up.
cards.use_when: Evaluating theme candidates before purchase or trial installation.

cards.title: Trial a Theme Before Buying to Preserve Work
cards.summary: Shopify lets you install a full theme trial, customize it, and buy later without losing changes.
cards.use_when: Deciding between finalist themes before committing to a purchase.

cards.title: Duplicate Your Theme as a Backup Before Big Changes
cards.summary: Duplicating the theme creates a safe restore point before customizations or updates.
cards.use_when: Before large theme edits, version pushes, or any risky change to a live storefront.

cards.title: Set Up a Password-Protected Coming Soon Page
cards.summary: Every Shopify store is password-locked by default and the 'password' theme controls what visitors see pre-launch.
cards.use_when: Preparing to launch a store or keep a site private while building it.

cards.title: Reject One-Click AI Whole-Store Theming; Design for Conversion
cards.summary: Shopify's instant AI store generator may shortchange the conversion-focused design work that a curated theme delivers.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to launch with an auto-generated theme or to design the storefront deliberately.

cards.title: Plan Theme Around Site Structure and Future Catalog
cards.summary: Theme choice is a multi-year decision — pick based on the features, sections, and catalog growth you expect, not just today's look.
cards.use_when: Committing to a theme for a store you plan to grow over years.

cards.title: Lock the store with password during setup and use it for early access
cards.summary: Every new Shopify store is password-protected by default; keep the lock until launch, or use it deliberately to give waitlist customers early access before the public launch.
cards.use_when: Launching or pre-launching your store, or running an early-access drop for waitlist subscribers.

cards.title: Edit products, collections and pages inside the theme editor
cards.summary: Modern Shopify lets you modify product, collection and page content from within the theme editor itself instead of bouncing back to the admin backend.
cards.use_when: Eyeballing a section and wanting to tweak the linked product, collection title/description or page content while you stay in visual edit mode.

cards.title: Navigate the theme editor: locations, pages, inspector and view modes
cards.summary: Orient within the Shopify theme editor—store location selector, page selector, inspector toggle, desktop/mobile/fullscreen views and undo/redo/save.
cards.use_when: Setting up your store theme and figuring out where to make changes and which page or market you're editing.

cards.title: Get a shareable preview link for draft and published themes
cards.summary: Draft themes expose a copyable preview link directly, but published themes require right-click-copy-link on the preview to share a mobile-testable URL.
cards.use_when: Testing your store on a real phone, or sending a work-in-progress theme to a client or teammate for review.

cards.title: Set brand colors once and connect theme colors to them via dynamic sources
cards.summary: Define a small palette in Shopify brand settings, then link theme color fields to those brand colors with dynamic sources so a palette change updates the whole theme at once.
cards.use_when: Setting up theme colors before launch, or rebranding, so a palette swap doesn't require hunting through every color field.

cards.title: Configure buttons, background, header and section color schemes
cards.summary: Set primary/secondary button styling, overall background, header colors and a small set of reusable section color schemes so sections can alternate backgrounds without a boring look.
cards.use_when: Merchandising your storefront design, and planning how homepage sections will visually alternate (light/dark backgrounds) across the store.

cards.title: Set typography, sizes and button shapes from theme settings
cards.summary: Configure heading/text/navigation fonts, font sizes and button rounding in one place, choosing fonts from Shopify's library to avoid custom coding.
cards.use_when: Setting up theme typography and button styling before launch, or tuning readability after seeing the store on desktop and mobile.

cards.title: Customize product cards: image shape, cropping, alignment and mobile per-row count
cards.summary: Control how product cards display—image aspect/crop behavior, alignment, text alignment, hover image, labels and mobile products per row—to keep product listings consistent.
cards.use_when: Setting up how products appear on homepage and collection listings; fixing a listing where mixed square/portrait product images look inconsistent.

cards.title: Set up header: announcement bar, sticky header and menus
cards.summary: Configure the header group—announcements with optional countdown and country/language selectors, logo sizing, sticky behavior and the main menu—while keeping it simple.
cards.use_when: Building the site-wide header that shoppers see on every page, including promo messaging and navigation.

cards.title: Build multi-level and mega menus that mirror how shoppers think
cards.summary: Structure multi-level and mega menus so the same product can be reached from multiple mental models (product type, activity, gender, etc.), matching how a reference retailer organizes navigation.
cards.use_when: Designing site navigation and collection hierarchy to help different shopper intents find products quickly.

cards.title: Configure cart behavior: drawer vs page and free shipping bar
cards.summary: Choose whether Add to cart opens a cart drawer or navigates to the cart page, and whether to add a free shipping bar, since it affects how easily shoppers keep browsing.
cards.use_when: Setting up cart experience before launch, and optimizing how customers proceed from product to checkout.

cards.title: Use currency formats, advanced settings and custom CSS carefully
cards.summary: Adjust price display via currency formats, review advanced filter/link options, and use theme-level custom CSS only to override display without touching theme files.
cards.use_when: Tweaking minor store display details (price formatting, filter and link behavior) or applying small display overrides without editing theme code.

cards.title: Use theme style presets as a starting point
cards.summary: Theme 'style' presets let you pick a pre-built demo layout as a starting base instead of building every section from scratch.
cards.use_when: Starting a new theme setup when you want a faster starting point and are willing to replace most section content anyway.

cards.title: Build the footer with link lists, blocks and policies
cards.summary: The footer is common across all pages; set its colors in theme settings, then add blocks such as text/logo, link lists and newsletter—linking to policies you generate in the backend.
cards.use_when: Building site-wide secondary navigation and policy links at launch, and deciding whether to include a newsletter signup in the footer.

cards.title: Build footer policy and support menus before linking them in the theme
cards.summary: Create Shopify policies and an About page first, then assemble two or three footer link menus and attach them as footer link-list blocks.
cards.use_when: Setting up the store footer so policy, contact and support pages are reachable from every page of the storefront.

cards.title: Choose theme sections by first checking the available section library
cards.summary: Inspect the theme's full section library and confirm niche-critical sections exist before committing to a theme.
cards.use_when: Selecting or trialling a Shopify theme, or planning which homepage/PDP/collection sections your store will need.

cards.title: Assemble the homepage in a deliberate section order
cards.summary: Build the homepage one section at a time in a sequence that moves from brand message to proof to bestsellers to story, removing theme defaults you don't need.
cards.use_when: Designing or rebuilding the store homepage structure after the header and footer are set.

cards.title: Set hero slideshow height and focal point to prevent bad crops
cards.summary: Control slideshow height, per-device images and image focal points so the hero looks intentional on desktop and mobile.
cards.use_when: Configuring a homepage hero slideshow or banner section where images crop awkwardly across devices.

cards.title: Use duplicate and copy-paste to build section sets quickly and consistently
cards.summary: Duplicate blocks to inherit identical dimensions, and copy entire sections between pages so shared layouts stay consistent.
cards.use_when: Building repetitive section structures such as logo lists, USP rows or cross-page content bands in the theme editor.

cards.title: Create a bestsellers collection with tags and feature it
cards.summary: Tag chosen products, build an automated tag-based bestsellers collection, and render it via a featured-collection section.
cards.use_when: Adding a bestsellers or curated homepage product row when the store has no existing bestsellers collection.

cards.title: Build automated collections with AND-style tag conditions
cards.summary: Create one collection from multiple tag conditions so products tagged with any of several values all appear in a single category.
cards.use_when: Building a parent category (e.g. all activewear) that should gather several product types tagged separately.

cards.title: Configure collection filters using Shopify Search & Discovery
cards.summary: Add product-type, size, colour and other filters via the Search & Discovery app, then make sure the underlying product data is populated.
cards.use_when: Setting up collection page filtering so shoppers can narrow a large catalogue by type, size, colour or price.

cards.title: Turn on colour swatches with defined colours or variant images
cards.summary: Expose variant colours on collection product cards using either named colour swatches with hex values or automatically pulled variant images.
cards.use_when: Collection-page merchandising when products come in multiple colours but the cards show no colour indication.

cards.title: Work on the default collection template first, then branch to custom templates
cards.summary: Set universal collection settings once in the default template, then create named templates for collections that need extra sections.
cards.use_when: Deciding between editing the shared default collection layout and creating per-collection layouts.

cards.title: Add a visual subcollection row with a multicolumn section
cards.summary: Simulate subcollection navigation by duplicating a multicolumn block per subcollection, each with image and link, at the top of a custom collection template.
cards.use_when: Large catalogues where a parent collection needs to route shoppers into leggings/bras/overalls-style subsections.

cards.title: Use collection metafields to vary content inside a shared collection template
cards.summary: Define collection metafields for image, title, text and link, then connect section fields to dynamic sources so one layout shows different promotional content per collection.
cards.use_when: Running one collection layout with a promotion or lookbook band whose content must differ per collection.

cards.title: Research competitor PDPs and reviews before designing your product page
cards.summary: Derive the sections and proof points for your product page from big competitors' structures and from customer questions and objections in reviews.
cards.use_when: Planning a product page layout or rewriting PDP content, especially before building a new template.

cards.title: Use Sidekick to make editor changes — with eyes open about scope
cards.summary: Ask Shopify's Sidekick to modify a section's settings from inside the theme editor, but verify that the change hasn't leaked into other sections.
cards.use_when: Making quick visual tweaks to a homepage or PDP section when you're not yet comfortable with theme settings.

cards.title: Mine competitor PDPs and reviews for objections
cards.summary: Reverse-engineer competitor product pages and review sections to surface the objections your own PDP must answer.
cards.use_when: Before writing or redesigning any product page, to decide what proof and information to include.

cards.title: Answer objections in proportion to price and complexity
cards.summary: Scale PDP information density to how complex, expensive or unfamiliar the product is.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much content a specific product page needs during PDP build-out.

cards.title: Repeat key information in multiple formats on the PDP
cards.summary: Present the same benefit or ingredient content in more than one visual format so different browsing styles find it.
cards.use_when: Designing PDP layout and section order after deciding what information to include.

cards.title: Decide product page templates by category vs. meta fields for per-product content
cards.summary: Use product templates for category-level layout differences and meta fields for content that must vary per product.
cards.use_when: Setting up a Shopify product page structure across a catalog with multiple product types.

cards.title: Configure Shopify product page section settings
cards.summary: Walk the product-page section settings that materially affect buyer behavior before adding content blocks.
cards.use_when: Initial setup of the product page in the theme editor on Shopify.

cards.title: Group variant images by color using theme logic
cards.summary: Make the gallery show only the images belonging to the selected variant.
cards.use_when: Setting up product media for a product sold in multiple colors.

cards.title: Place short benefit bullets and description above the buy button
cards.summary: Use a concise benefit list near the add-to-cart area to shorten the decision.
cards.use_when: Structuring the above-the-fold content of a product page.

cards.title: Deliver sizing confidence with a size chart page or meta field
cards.summary: Make a size guide accessible from the product page, choosing between a shared page and a per-product page meta field.
cards.use_when: Setting up apparel or any product where buyers hesitate about which size to pick.

cards.title: Use collapsible tabs for FAQ-type PDP content
cards.summary: Answer common pre-purchase questions in expandable tabs without lengthening the visible page.
cards.use_when: Adding fitting, care, shipping and returns information to a product page.

cards.title: Show fit/true-to-size rating when the theme supports it
cards.summary: Use a fit-rating feature to set sizing expectations and reduce size-related returns.
cards.use_when: Apparel PDPs where buyers are unsure whether to size up or down.

cards.title: Choose between Add to cart and Buy it now
cards.summary: Decide whether to keep the one-click buy button based on whether buyers typically purchase one item or several.
cards.use_when: Configuring the buy buttons on a Shopify product page.

cards.title: Set complimentary products to lift average order value
cards.summary: Curate 'goes with this' recommendations that feel like a helpful add-on to the current purchase.
cards.use_when: Configuring the complimentary products section on a product page to raise AOV.

cards.title: Add brand-trust and feature sections below the buy area
cards.summary: Reinforce positioning and product features beneath the main product section.
cards.use_when: Building the lower half of a product page after the core buy section is finished.

cards.title: Generate missing PDP sections with Shopify's AI section tool
cards.summary: Create sections your theme lacks, such as a comparison table, by prompting the built-in AI section generator.
cards.use_when: When your theme library is missing a section you need on a product page (comparison table, custom layout).

cards.title: Design the collections list ('all collections') page
cards.summary: Structure a page that lists collections, grouped logically instead of dumping every collection.
cards.use_when: Setting up navigation for a store with many collections or categories.

cards.title: Keep the cart page and cart drawer simple
cards.summary: Avoid over-engineering the cart; small copy and setting tweaks are usually enough.
cards.use_when: Reviewing the cart page or cart drawer in theme settings.

cards.title: Build richer static pages with templates instead of plain text
cards.summary: Turn flat pages like About Us into designed pages by creating templates and assigning them.
cards.use_when: Creating or upgrading About Us, story or other static content pages.

cards.title: Organize content into multiple blog families
cards.summary: Use separate blogs to keep distinct content types organized and linkable.
cards.use_when: Setting up a store blog with more than one content theme (e.g. recipes vs. health facts for a grocery store).

cards.title: Customize search, password and error pages
cards.summary: Cover the remaining theme pages that affect visitor experience outside the core funnel.
cards.use_when: Finishing theme setup after homepage, product, collection, cart and static pages.

cards.title: Expect limited checkout customization outside Shopify Plus
cards.summary: Set expectations for what you can change on the checkout and customer account pages.
cards.use_when: Planning checkout or account-page changes on a standard Shopify plan.

cards.title: Locked Shopify Checkout: What You Can Adjust Without Plus
cards.summary: Non-Plus Shopify stores have a locked checkout, so plan customizations around the few available settings, apps and page blocks.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much checkout customization to attempt on a standard (non-Plus) Shopify store before spending time or budget on it.

cards.title: Configure Contact Method and Required Fields at Checkout
cards.summary: Choose email-only contact collection and set field requirements at checkout to maximize email capture without adding friction.
cards.use_when: Setting up the checkout form fields in Shopify checkout settings for a new store or auditing an existing one for data capture.

cards.title: Separate Transactional Consent From Marketing Consent at Checkout
cards.summary: A customer giving you an email for order delivery has not consented to marketing — use the checkout subscribe checkbox and pre-select it only where legally allowed.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to present email/SMS marketing opt-in at checkout, and which regions should have it pre-selected.

cards.title: Turn On Abandoned Checkout Recovery Emails
cards.summary: Activate Shopify's built-in abandoned checkout email, or route abandoned checkout flows through your email platform, to recover sales.
cards.use_when: Setting up post-checkout-abandon recovery for a new store or deciding whether Shopify or an external ESP should own the flow.

cards.title: Limit Quantity Per Order to Protect Inventory
cards.summary: Shopify's advanced checkout preferences let you cap how many items a customer can add or buy at once, useful for scarce stock or limited drops.
cards.use_when: Protecting limited inventory from single large orders, or keeping stock counts less obvious during a limited release.

cards.title: Configure the Customer Account Page and Its Domain
cards.summary: Choose Shopify's modern passcode-based customer accounts, brand the account/login URL, and enable new account features like self-returns and store credits.
cards.use_when: Setting up or upgrading the customer account experience — login method, order history, returns and branding — for a Shopify store.

cards.title: Choose Discount Code vs Automatic Discount
cards.summary: Decide between a typed discount code and an automatic discount based on whether you need attribution, distribution, or zero-friction application.
cards.use_when: Creating a Shopify discount for a promotion, influencer campaign, welcome flow or sitewide sale.

cards.title: Share a Pre-Applied Discount Link Instead of a Code
cards.summary: Shopify discount codes can be delivered as shareable links so the discount applies automatically at checkout, reducing customer steps.
cards.use_when: Sending promotions by email, SMS or ads where you want the discount applied without the customer typing anything.

cards.title: Know Shopify's Gap Limit and When to Add a Discount App
cards.summary: Shopify's native discounts cannot cap the maximum amount saved (e.g. 30% off up to $100), which matters most for high-AOV stores.
cards.use_when: Designing percentage-off promotions for a store with a high average order value, where uncapped savings would be too costly.

cards.title: Set Up a Gift Card Product for Last-Minute Buyers
cards.summary: Create a gift card product with preset denominations so customers can buy a gift when shipping can no longer arrive in time.
cards.use_when: Adding gift cards as a product, especially ahead of holidays or any period when delivery timelines will miss the occasion.

cards.title: Choosing and Vetting Shopify Apps Before Committing
cards.summary: Evaluate apps by reviews, demo store and support responsiveness rather than by feature claims, since poor apps look good on paper.
cards.use_when: Selecting any Shopify app — reviews, bundles, subscriptions, upsells, loyalty — for a store you operate or manage.

cards.title: Install a Review App and Collect Reviews by Email
cards.summary: Use a review app that emails past customers a post-purchase review request so reviews accumulate with low friction.
cards.use_when: Adding social proof to product pages on a new or growing Shopify store and deciding which review app to use.

cards.title: Add Bundling and Subscription Apps Only Where the Niche Supports Them
cards.summary: Bundles raise average order value in most niches; subscriptions only make sense for consumables and repeat-need products.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add bundle listings or subscription options to a Shopify store's catalog.
